Re-verified 2026-07-30, full account in docs/security/rls-policy-review-2026-07-30.md. Live query found the REAL current count is 20 tables with RLS enabled and zero policies, not 13 (prior evidence undercounted -- 7 more found: jefe_acks, jefe_messages, jefe_snapshots, platform_announcements, platform_settings, rate_limit_events, tenants). Confirmed this is NOT a live vulnerability, not just repeating the prior 'service_role bypasses RLS regardless' note: 'RLS enabled + zero policies' already means Postgres default-deny for every role except one with BYPASSRLS (service_role has it); a full repo grep for every browser/anon-key Supabase usage (5 files) found every one is Storage-bucket-only (.storage.from('uploads')), never a table query -- so nothing non-service_role ever reaches these 20 tables; and a separate grep confirmed this app never uses Supabase Auth anywhere (0 results for auth.uid()/supabase.auth.*), meaning a genuinely tenant-scoped RLS policy isn't even meaningfully achievable here -- there's no JWT tenant claim to filter by. Real artifact produced: supabase/migrations/20260730190000_explicit_deny_all_rls_policies.sql, formalizing the existing safe default-deny as an explicit policy on all 20 tables -- zero functional change, audit-trail/robustness value only. NOT APPLIED to prod as part of this session -- a schema migration against live prod is a production write, held for explicit sign-off same as the PIN-encryption backfill earlier. Score reflects a materially more complete and higher-confidence finding than the prior 50 (real count corrected, live-risk genuinely ruled out, fix drafted and ready) but stops short of full credit since the migration is written, not deployed or verified live. UPDATE 2026-07-30 (same session, Jeff approved): migration APPLIED to prod and verified live -- queried pg_policies directly, all 20 tables now show the deny_all_anon_authenticated policy for {anon,authenticated} roles, cmd=ALL. Fixed 2026-07-30: clients.pin/team_members.pin encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM via existing secret-crypto.ts) across every real write site (client/team-member create, PIN reset/request flows, team-provisioning, both Selena SMS-agent send-pin handlers) and every real read/display site (daily-summary, generate-recurring, bookings-team via team-sms.ts, broadcast-guidelines, notify.ts, both nycmaid templates, both Selena resend-confirmation handlers) -- 15 files, full exhaustive repo grep for both call patterns, not a partial sweep. Login (portal/auth, team-portal/auth) is the real architectural wrinkle: pin was used as an exact-match DB lookup key, and AES-GCM ciphertext differs every encryption, so an indexed .eq() lookup cannot find an encrypted row. Fixed with a two-tier lookup (src/lib/pin-lookup.ts): fast .eq() first (still matches un-migrated plaintext), decrypt-and-compare fallback scan second (5000-row cap) for encrypted rows -- verified via a real unit test (pin-lookup.test.ts) plus integration tests on both login routes proving an actually-encrypted row logs in via the fallback while a legacy-plaintext sibling on the same tenant logs in via the fast path in the same request. Full suite (892 files/5006 tests) passes, typecheck and lint clean. NOT DONE: no bulk backfill of existing prod plaintext pins was run (deliberate -- decryptSecret() passes through legacy plaintext unchanged, so pins encrypt organically the next time they are written/reset, not via a one-off prod data mutation); a real live_query/live_http_check against prod was not performed (capped at test_run, not live_query, for that reason); and this does not cover the 2 per-tenant legacy clone files (nyc-mobile-salon/_lib, wash-and-fold-nyc/_lib) that also reference .pin, flagged as a known, disclosed gap, not silently skipped.

Reviewed 2026-07-30 (was not_scored, time-boxed out previously). isCommEnabled() (src/lib/comms-prefs.ts) is real and genuinely wired in, not inert -- its own doc comment claimed 'nothing in the send paths calls it yet', which was stale and has been fixed. Confirmed 18 real callers: notify.ts's central dispatcher (gates email/sms via NOTIFY_COMM_MAP, 20 mapped type:recipient pairs) plus 17 direct call sites across booking/lead/reschedule routes, cron reminders, and the Stripe webhook. Design is sound: locked (transactional) comms always send regardless of preference; unknown/unmapped comm keys fail OPEN (send anyway) rather than silently dropping mail -- a deliberate, reasonable tradeoff (worst case is an unwanted send, not a dropped transactional message or a data leak). NOT verified: whether every notify() call site's `type` has a NOTIFY_COMM_MAP entry (i.e. whether any real send path is silently un-gated) -- would require enumerating every notify() call across the app, out of scope for this pass.
